biography.plain_text: The government of the Republic of China (Taiwan) is the public authority responsible for national administration and local self-government in Taiwan. Rooted in a democratic constitution, it delivers public policy through central institutions and elected territorial governments. Its enduring remit spans legislation, administration, courts, civil service, public accountability and local services.

long_biography.plain_text:
Taiwan’s constitutional order rests on popular sovereignty and a division of responsibilities between central and local government. The president serves as head of state, while the Executive Yuan is the highest administrative body and works with the Legislative Yuan on laws, budgets and national policy. Separate Judicial, Examination and Control Yuans oversee courts, the civil service, impeachment and public audit.

Below the central level, the Local Government Act structures special municipalities, counties and cities as self-governing bodies. Councils exercise local legislative authority, while elected mayors and magistrates lead administration. This framework makes the government a system of constitutional institutions rather than a single agency or officeholder.

uncertainties.detail: Taiwan Government is a broad umbrella label, not the formal name of one uniquely identified ministry, branch or public corporation. The biography therefore describes the Republic of China (Taiwan)'s central and local public-administration system without narrowing the record to the Executive Yuan or another specific organ.

The source stores Taiwan and Government in first-name and surname fields and assigns nationality, residence, birth-country and mortality values, but these are artefacts of a person-shaped database. No middle name, gender, birth detail, personal title or mortality correction is proposed for the institution.

Official sources use Republic of China (Taiwan), while the immutable display label says Taiwan Government. The dossier preserves the source label and uses the official formulation in explanatory text without proposing a display-name change that might imply a more specific legal entity than the evidence supports.

The institutional classification does not identify a natural owner, officeholder, ministry, agency or ultimate decision-maker behind the source entry. Current political leaders are intentionally omitted so the text remains durable and does not convert a public institution into a personal record.

Schema v8 requires all four wealth labels to remain Unknown for institutions. Institution records cannot propose personal or organisational socials, so official government domains are preserved as sources rather than imported as Company Website or personal-social records.

Government-owned is the only minimum useful active tag whose catalogue contract explicitly includes a record that is itself a government or sovereign public entity. Public-office and government-contracting tags describe people or business models and are not proposed.

Private assets, registries, travel, residences, security-sensitive detail, changing officeholders, political advocacy, sovereignty disputes and transient policy claims are excluded from the biography, classifications, tag and proposal.
